quests.instruction: Which of these animals sleeps the least, often napping in short bursts?
quests.hint: Two of these animals are famous snoozers. This one is not.
quests.explanation: Giraffes sleep only a few hours a day, in short naps, and they can nap standing up. Koalas and sloths sleep for much longer.
quests.funFact: A resting giraffe sometimes folds its long neck back along its body.
quests.question: Giraffe

quests.instruction: Which animal can spend winter buried in pond mud or leaf litter, with its body slowed right down?
quests.hint: It stays still until warm weather comes back.
quests.explanation: Many frogs spend cold weather hidden in mud or under leaves, hardly moving, and take in a little oxygen through their skin.
quests.funFact: Some wood frogs can survive with parts of their bodies frozen solid.
quests.question: Frog

quests.instruction: Name the animal that can sleep on a branch without falling off, because its toes lock around the perch.
quests.hint: A tightening in its legs holds its grip, even when it's asleep.
quests.explanation: When a bird crouches, tendons in its legs tighten and lock its toes around the perch, so it holds on without trying.
quests.funFact: Many small birds fluff up and tuck their bills into their back feathers when they sleep.
quests.question: Songbird

quests.instruction: Which insect works through the daylight hours, visiting flowers, then rests in the hive at night?
quests.hint: Its working day ends when it gets dark.
quests.explanation: Honey bees fly out in daylight to find flowers and rest in the hive at night.
quests.funFact: Bees can see ultraviolet light, which shows patterns on flowers that we can't see.
quests.question: Bee

quests.instruction: Which spiky garden visitor trundles around at night looking for slugs and beetles?
quests.hint: You're more likely to hear it than see it.
quests.explanation: Hedgehogs are nocturnal. They sleep in a nest by day, and come out after dark to hunt for slugs, worms and beetles.
quests.funFact: A hedgehog can walk a couple of kilometres in a single night.
quests.question: Hedgehog

quests.instruction: Find the animal that is most active at dawn and dusk, when the light is dim and the air is cooler.
quests.hint: It avoids both the midday heat and the deepest dark.
quests.explanation: Rabbits are most active around dawn and dusk. Midday is too hot and bright, and the middle of the night is when many hunters are about.
quests.funFact: Rabbits eat their soft droppings a second time to get nutrients they missed the first time.
quests.question: Rabbit

quests.instruction: Find the sea animal that carries a sponge over its snout to protect it while it searches the sandy sea floor.
quests.hint: The sponge works like a tiny glove.
quests.explanation: Some dolphins in Australia put sponges over their snouts as protection while hunting. It is a clever way to use a tool.
quests.funFact: Dolphin mothers pass the sponge habit on to their calves.
quests.question: Dolphin

quests.instruction: Spot the huge animal that can break off a branch and use it as a fly swatter.
quests.hint: It uses its trunk to hold the branch.
quests.explanation: Elephants have been seen using branches to swat flies and to scratch themselves.
quests.funFact: Elephants can recognise themselves in a mirror, which only a few animals can do.
quests.question: Elephant

quests.instruction: Which clever sea animal sometimes carries half a coconut shell and uses it as a portable hideout?
quests.hint: It finds a shelter and takes it along.
quests.explanation: Some octopuses carry coconut shells and hide inside them when danger comes near. This is a rare example of an animal using a tool.
quests.funFact: An octopus can learn to unscrew a jar lid to get at food inside.
quests.question: Octopus

quests.instruction: Find the farm bird that scratches a hollow in dry dirt and ruffles in the dust to keep clean.
quests.hint: Dust soaks up extra oil and helps shake out tiny pests.
quests.explanation: Chickens take dust baths. Dust helps clean their feathers and get rid of pests.
quests.funFact: A chicken can run about as fast as a person jogging.
quests.question: Chicken

quests.instruction: Which animals pick through each other's fur to remove dirt and tiny pests, and to build friendships?
quests.hint: It's a kind of teamwork called grooming.
quests.explanation: Monkeys groom each other to keep clean, and grooming helps them stay friends.
quests.funFact: Grooming helps monkeys feel calm and relaxed.
quests.question: Monkey

quests.instruction: Which pet's tongue is covered with tiny backward-pointing hooks that work like a hairbrush?
quests.hint: A lick feels like sandpaper.
quests.explanation: A cat's rough tongue has tiny hooks that comb loose fur and dirt as it grooms.
quests.funFact: Cats can spend about a third of their waking time grooming.
quests.question: Cat

quests.instruction: Young animals pounce, stalk and wrestle in play. Which animal's cubs learn to hunt this way?
quests.hint: Games that look like fun are really hunting practice.
quests.explanation: Playing helps lion cubs practise stalking and pouncing safely before they need those skills for real.
quests.funFact: Lion cubs are born with spots that fade as they grow up.
quests.question: Lion

quests.instruction: Which farm animal loves to leap and balance on rocks, logs and fences?
quests.hint: Its split hooves grip small ledges.
quests.explanation: Goats are curious climbers. Jumping and climbing builds their balance and strength.
quests.funFact: People have kept goats for around ten thousand years.
quests.question: Goat

quests.instruction: Spot the small animal that makes high-pitched chirps, too high for us to hear, when it is tickled or plays.
quests.hint: Scientists need special microphones to hear its giggles.
quests.explanation: Rats make ultrasonic chirps when they play and are tickled. It is a sound too high for people to hear.
quests.funFact: Some rats are trained to sniff out hidden items by smell.
quests.question: Rat

quests.instruction: Name the small animal that remembers where it buried hundreds of nuts, and sometimes pretends to bury one to fool onlookers.
quests.hint: It's a bit of a trickster with its snacks.
quests.explanation: Squirrels remember many hiding spots. Sometimes they pretend to bury a nut to mislead anyone watching.
quests.funFact: Squirrels forget some nuts, which can grow into new trees.
quests.question: Squirrel

quests.instruction: Which animal's memory helps its group find waterholes it visited many years ago?
quests.hint: Older members of the group remember where to go in a drought.
quests.explanation: Elephants can remember where food and water were found, and older females lead the group there.
quests.funFact: An elephant's brain is the biggest of any land animal.
quests.question: Elephant

quests.instruction: Which animal can learn the names of many toys and fetch them on request?
quests.hint: One famous example learned more than a thousand names.
quests.explanation: Dogs can learn many words and signals. A border collie named Chaser knew more than a thousand toy names.
quests.funFact: Dogs can read human hand signals, such as pointing.
quests.question: Dog

quests.instruction: In some kinds of this bird, the male gives his partner a smooth pebble as a gift. Which bird?
quests.hint: Pebbles are valuable for building nests on rocky ground.
quests.explanation: In some penguin species, a male presents a pebble to his partner. Pebbles are used to build the nest.
quests.funFact: A penguin pair may fight over a good pebble.
quests.question: Penguin

quests.instruction: Which long-legged birds march together in a group, turning their heads at the same time, to find a partner?
quests.hint: They move like a pink parade.
quests.explanation: Flamingos gather and march in a group, turning their heads together, which is a dance that helps them choose mates.
quests.funFact: Flamingos feed their chick with a special milky liquid made in their throats.
quests.question: Flamingo

quests.instruction: Which animal roars to warn rivals that this land is already taken?
quests.hint: The sound can travel for kilometres.
quests.explanation: A lion's roar carries a long way, telling other lions whose territory they're entering.
quests.funFact: A lion's roar can be heard from about eight kilometres away.
quests.question: Lion

quests.instruction: Find the small reef swimmer that picks pests off larger sea animals in return for a meal.
quests.hint: Larger sea animals wait their turn to be cleaned by it.
quests.explanation: Cleaner fish eat pests from the skin of larger fish. The big fish gets cleaner, and the cleaner gets fed.
quests.funFact: On coral reefs, big fish sometimes queue at "cleaning stations".
quests.question: Tropical Fish

quests.instruction: Which insect "farms" tiny sap-sucking aphids and collects their sweet droplets?
quests.hint: It guards its herd from hungry beetles.
quests.explanation: Ants protect aphids from enemies. In return, aphids give them a sugary liquid called honeydew.
quests.funFact: Some ants grow fungus in their nests and eat it.
quests.question: Ant

quests.instruction: Name the night flier that visits cactus flowers and carries pollen from one flower to the next.
quests.hint: Pollen sticks to its fur as it drinks nectar.
quests.explanation: Some bats drink nectar from night-blooming flowers. Pollen sticks to their fur and is carried to the next flower.
quests.funFact: Bats help pollinate plants that give us fruits such as bananas.
quests.question: Bat

quests.instruction: Find the huge animal that opens its mouth wide to show off enormous teeth and warn a rival.
quests.hint: That yawn isn't sleepiness.
quests.explanation: A hippo's wide-open mouth is a warning. It shows off its huge teeth to a rival.
quests.funFact: A hippo's big lower canine teeth can grow to about half a metre long.
quests.question: Hippo

quests.instruction: Find the farm bird that fans its tail and puffs up its feathers to look bigger and more impressive.
quests.hint: He's trying to look as large as he can.
quests.explanation: A male turkey puffs up his feathers and fans his tail to impress females and frighten rivals.
quests.funFact: The loose red skin on a turkey's throat is called a wattle, and it changes colour with the turkey's mood.
quests.question: Turkey

quests.instruction: Spot the animal that stays active all winter and keeps hunting in the snow, instead of sleeping through the cold.
quests.hint: Two of these animals take a long winter sleep.
quests.explanation: Wolves don't hibernate. A thick double coat keeps them warm as they hunt through winter.
quests.funFact: A wolf's winter coat has a soft warm undercoat and long water-repelling outer hairs.
quests.question: Wolf

quests.instruction: Name the sea mammal that can hold its breath for an hour or more while diving deeper than a kilometre.
quests.hint: It stores oxygen in its muscles and blood.
quests.explanation: Some whales, like sperm whales, dive very deep and stay under for an hour or longer, using oxygen stored in their muscles and blood.
quests.funFact: Sperm whales have the biggest brain of any animal on Earth.
quests.question: Whale

quests.instruction: Which large water bird often keeps the same partner for years and returns to the same nesting place?
quests.hint: Pairs of these birds often stay together for many years.
quests.explanation: Many swan pairs stay together for years and come back to the same nesting site.
quests.funFact: A swan pair may add to the same nest year after year.
quests.question: Swan

quests.instruction: Find the small bird that tilts its head to one side on a lawn because its eyes are on the sides of its head.
quests.hint: It's looking at the ground with one eye at a time.
quests.explanation: Robins have eyes on the sides of their heads, so they tilt them to look at the ground with one eye.
quests.funFact: A European robin can sense Earth's magnetic field, which helps it find its way.
quests.question: Robin
